grammar.title: Inversion After Negative Adverbials
grammar.explanation:
In a normal English sentence, the subject comes before the verb. Inversion flips that order after certain negative words at the start of a sentence.

Use inversion after **never**, **rarely**, **seldom**, and **hardly ever** when they open a sentence. The helper verb comes before the subject, which gives the sentence a formal, dramatic tone.

Use inversion after **not only** and **not until** as well. **Not only** usually pairs with **but also** later in the same sentence, as in a review of a bespoke collection.

Use inversion after **no sooner** and **little** too. **No sooner** pairs with **than**, and **little did** is a common storytelling opener.

Inversion sounds formal and dramatic. It suits essays, speeches, and storytelling, and it can give a sartorial review or a couture report real punch.
examples: *Never have I seen* such a flamboyant gown at a couture show. (inversion after never)
*Rarely does* a bespoke suit fail to impress. (inversion after rarely)
*Not only is* the silhouette elegant, but the fabric also drapes beautifully. (not only ... but also)
*Little did* the designer know that her eclectic collection would win the prize. (inversion after little)
*No sooner had* the capsule collection launched *than* it sold out. (no sooner ... than)
*Seldom has* an understated dress received so much praise. (inversion after seldom)

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: I have never seen such sartorial elegance.
practice.a: Never have I seen such sartorial elegance.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: The couture gown rarely fails to impress.
practice.a: Rarely does the couture gown fail to impress.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: The designer had hardly finished the embellishments when the show began.
practice.a: Hardly had the designer finished the embellishments when the show began.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: The capsule collection was not only practical but also stylish.
practice.a: Not only was the capsule collection practical, but it was also stylish.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: I little knew that the eclectic outfit would become a trend.
practice.a: Little did I know that the eclectic outfit would become a trend.
